newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris financial markets mull Dec 31, 1998 close.
newsitem.headline: Paris financial markets mull Dec 31, 1998 close.

text.p: Financial market participants here are considering closing market activity on December 31, 1998 to allow enough time to switch to a single European currency, Banque Paribas board member Dominique Hoenn said on Wednesday.

Hoenn, part of a working group dealing with preparations for introduction of the euro, told a Paris Europlace conference "we are contemplating having four days available, and if we close (an extra day) it will (be) on December 31. But the decision has not been taken yet."
The single currency is due to be launched on Friday, January 1, 1999. A bank holiday would mean January 4 will be the first trading day in the new currency.
Hoenn said he thought it would be difficult to manage the switch in three days, although Paris was waiting to see what other countries planned to do before deciding.
"If we close, it will be everything," Hoenn said. If that were the case, positions at the end of trading on December 30 would form the basis for conversion into a single currency, he said.
